'''Trowee Astur''' was a light-skinned [[human]] who worked as a [[haulcraft]] [[pilot]] during the [[High Republic Era]]. They [[Transport|shuttled]] passengers and cargo from an [[Ueda orbital station|orbital station]] above the [[planet]] [[Ueda]] that housed the world's [[Ueda trade commission|trade commission]].<ref name="AcolyteVG" /> In [[132 BBY]],<ref name="Date">{{TheAcolyteDate}}</ref> Astur stood beside<ref name="LostFound">{{Acolyte|Lost / Found}}</ref> the [[herbalist]] [[Reya Nell]]<ref name="AcolyteVG" /> at a stall just inside the gate of<ref name="LostFound" /> [[Point Ueda]]—the [[capital]] [[city]] of Ueda<ref name="AcolyteVG" />—as the [[Sith assassin]] [[Mae-ho Aniseya]] [[Mae's quest|entered]] through the gateway. While at the stall,<ref name="LostFound" /> the pilot wore a [[Color|brown]] [[jacket]] with [[Hair|fur]]-covered shoulders, a brown [[hat]] lined with [[Nerf-wool|Nerf-fur]], gray pants, and brown [[murra-leather]] [[boot]]s. They had a brown [[bandolier]] and a [[C-44D "Piratesweeper" blaster rifle]] slung over their shoulder.<ref name="AcolyteVG" />

==Behind the scenes==
Trowee Astur first appeared in "[[Lost / Found]],"<ref name="LostFound" /> the first episode of the live-action television series ''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'', which aired on [[Disney+]] on [[June 4]], [[2024]].<ref name="Announcement">{{SW|url=news/the-acolyte-teaser-poster|text=''The Acolyte'' Teaser Poster, Premiere Date Revealed}}</ref> Prior to the release of the episode, Astur was revealed in a trailer exclusively shown at [[Celebration Europe (2023)|Celebration Europe]]<ref name="Celebration">{{CelebrationTrailer|''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte]]''|Celebration Europe (2023)}}</ref> during the [[Lucasfilm]] Studio Showcase on [[April 7]], [[2023]].<ref name="CelebrationDate">{{SW|url=news/swce-2023-lucasfilm-studio-showcase|text=SWCE 2023: 11 Highlights from Lucasfilm's Studio Showcase}}</ref> The character is visible in concept art of the Ueda Village Gate created by [[Kevin Jenkins]] and [[Stephen Tappin]].<ref name="ArtOf">''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Acolyte]]''</ref> The Ueda gate scene was shot at [[Shinfield Studios]],<ref name="Fantha Part I">{{WebCite|url=https://www.fanthatracks.com/news/the-acolyte-a-journey-to-the-filming-locations-part-1-madeira|text=The Acolyte: A journey to the filming locations Part 1: Madeira|archivedate=20241204220147}}</ref> [[Wikipedia:England|England]].<ref name="Julian Foddy">{{Lucasfilm|url=news/julian-foddy-acolyte|text=''The Acolyte'' Visual Effects Supervisor Julian Foddy}}</ref> The pilot was then identified in the [[2025]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte: The Visual Guide]]'', which was written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]].<ref name="AcolyteVG" />
